text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: autoscaler failure in dedicated-us-west-2. GPU pool 'redwood-dedicated-1' hit capacity limit and failed to scale. queue_size=12,842, 5xx_rate +7% over 5m. paging oncall-dan.

nova-deploy-bot: Deploy started: model=redwood-ost-2.1 rollout=20% -> 80% (canary->prod). Noted increased memory allotment per worker.

oncall-dan: seeing the page, taking it. joining bridge. 

oncall-dan: quick sanity: is this correlated with the rollout? @ryan-ml can you confirm?

ryan-ml: yes. metrics show per-request GPU mem jumped ~30% after 2.1 due to longer kv-cache allocation for extended context. throughput per-GPU down ~25%.

maria-sre: queue growth looks like exponential since ~10:12 UTC. autoscaler tried 3 scale attempts and hit project-level GPU quota. logs: `autoscaler: scale_up_failed: quota_exceeded`.

alex-eng: customers impacted: increase in 5xx and request latency. support reported 12+ SEV tickets in last 30m. @support-lead can you confirm severity?

support-lead: confirmed. two high-priority customers on dedicated instances reported timeouts and degraded throughput. They're hitting timeouts at 30s. We're triaging and notifying customers.

emily-pm: what's the blast radius? Which tenants on dedicated-us-west-2?

maria-sre: tenants A, B, and C (reserved capacity). Also some hosted traffic was routed to fallbacks in same region causing extra load.

ryan-ml: suspicion: OST 2.1 increased kv-cache per convo because default context fallback enabled. Combined with higher prompt lengths from a client, kv-cache retention increased and we started OOM/slowdowns.

oncall-dan: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) pause rollout and revert traffic to 2.0. 2) lower rollout % to 0% (force rollback). 3) manually request quota bump (slow). 4) emergency scale via spare pool in eu-central. 5) temporarily disable kv-cache on 2.1 or limit context length.

ryan-ml: I can trigger a rollback of the rollout to 2.0 and flip routing in ~3min. That should reduce per-GPU mem and throughput regression.

alex-eng: manual scaling: infra has spare nodes but autoscaler isn't attaching them due to quota. I can spin up ephemeral instances in a different account/region but that's a last resort.

oncall-dan: do rollback now. Prioritize rollback + route older model. Then we decide on node-level mitigations.

ryan-ml: rolling back. command: ```
# rollback rollout
curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood.internal/api/rollouts/rollback 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-ost","target_version":"2.0"}' 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN"
```

nova-deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by ryan-ml. starting traffic re-route.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty runbook step 2 triggered: reduce concurrency on affected service. Applying limit to 8 concurrent streams per worker.

maria-sre: applying concurrency cap now: ```
# set concurrency limit
kubectl -n inference patch deployment inference-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"MAX_CONCURRENCY","value":"8"}]}]}}}}'
```

alex-eng: caps in place. also dropped worker prefetch buffer from 1024 -> 256 which should reduce burst memory.

support-lead: update: SEV ticket from Customer A says latency improved slightly but still seeing timeouts.

oncall-dan: what's the queue size now?

maria-sre: queue_size=4,120 and trending down after rollback traffic routing started. 5xx delta now +1.2%. 

ryan-ml: rollback completed. routing at 100% -> 2.0. New model tasks draining.

emily-pm: good. what's next for root cause and preventions?

ryan-ml: immediate RCA notes: 2.1 changed KV-cache allocation behavior (kept extra context length in memory by default). Need to add a memory-safety flag and a model-compatibility check to rollout pipeline. Also add preflight test that runs a synthetic workload matching customer context lengths.

maria-sre: follow-ups for SRE: 1) autoscaler should surface quota_exceeded to ops channel earlier and block rollout if quota low. 2) add a circuit breaker for queue length > 5k to pause risky rollouts.

alex-eng: we should also enforce per-deployment RESERVED_QUOTA guardrails so we don't take entire region. I'll open infra ticket.

support-lead: customer comms: drafting an incident message explaining rollback and mitigation. will send within 30m.

oncall-dan: handing on-call to maria-sre at 11:05 UTC for follow-up. maria, you're now primary. I'll stay on standby. :thumbsup:

maria-sre: ack. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate infra tickets. adding notes to incident timeline.

ryan-ml: quick note: can we add a temporary flag to disable kv-cache for 2.1 in case we need to re-promote it? That would be less disruptive than a full rollback next time.

alex-eng: yes, we can. follow-up task: expose KV_CACHE_MAX_SIZE env var per-service and put default lower for canaries.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial. queue draining. rollback succeeded. assigning incident P0 -> P1 for postmortem.

support-lead: customer update drafted and sent to affected accounts. BTW one customer asked for timeline on when 2.1 will be safe to re-run.

emily-pm: timeline: let's plan a gated re-rollout after we implement kv safeguards + preflight tests, aim 72h.

maria-sre: last check: queue_size=1,002. 5xx rate back to baseline. closing active paging. I'll create postmortem and link PRs.

oncall-dan: thanks team. leaving final notes in incident channel.

maria-sre: posting postmortem draft in #postmortems and adding owners: ryan-ml (root cause), alex-eng (infra guardrails), maria-sre (monitoring/autoscaler).

support-lead: customers notified, follow-ups scheduled.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Duration ~48m.
